newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MPs urge return of Elgin marbles to Greece.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs urge return of Elgin marbles to Greece.

text.p: Over 250 members of the European Parliament -- more than a third -- have called for the return of the Elgin Marbles to Greece by Britain, saying they are a crucial part of Greek history and culture.
"I believe there will be very strong pressure to return the sculptures to their proper place and not the British Museum," British Socialist deputy Alf Lomas told a news conference.

The Greek government has asked the British government for talks on the return of the statues, which were taken from the Parthenon temple in Athens in 1806 by British diplomat Thomas Bruce, the 7th earl of Elgin.
Greek deputy Alexandros Alavanos said the statues are the heart of the country.
"They are in a jewel box in London but not in the body where they should be," he told the news conference.

But the British position has remained firm -- the statues belong to the British Museum and cannot be moved without an act of Parliament. The British government has said it has no intention of raising the issue.
Lomas said British opposition leader Tony Blair had ordered deputies from his Labour party not to sign the statement, an order ignored by most of them.

Elgin said he bought the marbles to preserve them. The marble statues date from the 5th century BC and are from the frieze and tympani of the Parthenon, which is considered the masterpiece of Greek architecture.

Lomas said that following a television programme in Britain 92 per cent of British people polled said they supported their return, providing it was not regarded as a precedent -- a term to which the Greek government has agreed.
A new museum is being built in the Acropolis to receive them and keep them in good condition.
